=You are the script editor of a {{ $('Genre Profile').first().json.p.format }}. Below is the complete draft narration of the film. Make it a story a viewer can follow easily and enjoy — coherent, forward-moving, never repetitive — while keeping everything that already works.
{{ $json.editorFeedback ? '\nCORRECTIONS REQUIRED BY THE PREVIOUS PASS — fix these first, then everything else:\n' + $json.editorFeedback + '\n' : '' }}
THE STORY SPINE the film must tell:
{{ JSON.stringify(($('Generate Outline').first().json.output || {}).story_spine || {}) }}

THE CHAPTER PLAN (each chapter's ENDS WITH / LEADS INTO lines are where its story lands):
{{ (($('Generate Outline').first().json.output || {}).chapters || []).map(c => 'CHAPTER ' + c.chapter_number + ': ' + c.chapter_title + '\n' + c.chapter_summary).join('\n\n') }}

EDIT FOR, in this order of importance:
1. REPETITION — the single biggest defect. Any fact, date, number, character introduction, place description, image or phrase that appears more than once stays ONLY where it works best and is removed everywhere else; a later mention may be a three-word reference, never a restatement. A chapter that re-opens the same scene, "returns to" earlier material or recaps is rewritten to move the story forward instead.
2. FRAGMENTS AND INVENTORIES — lists of objects and one-to-four-word fragments ("Worn floors. Old fixtures.") become actions somebody takes, or go.
2b. DESCRIPTION — the viewer is already watching the picture. Any sentence that tells them what they can see (an appearance, a surface, a colour, light, weather, a camera position, the motion of things for its own sake — "Rain needles the avenue", "the road climbs above the river, slick under flashing lamps", "sparks spit through spray") is replaced by what the picture CANNOT say about that moment — the intent, the stake, the cost, the cause, the consequence — or cut outright. A named place or time may stay; a described one may not. Real scripts carry zero texture words per hundred and a guard counts them.
3. THROUGHLINE — every chapter advances the spine's turning points in order; a beat that does not change the protagonist's situation is cut or replaced with an EVENT from the spine or the chapter plan.
4. TRANSITIONS — each chapter ends on its ENDS WITH beat and the next opens where the previous one led; the viewer always knows when and where they are.
4b. THE ENDING — the last chapter must finish on a CLOSING BEAT of two or three sentences: the final event and the consequence that outlives it, answering the question the film opened with in the film's own particulars. If the draft simply stops — most often on a camera line, a trailing "while…" or "as…" clause describing where things rest — write the close. It is the one place meaning may be stated aloud, and it is still not a summary of the chapters, not a moral addressed to the viewer and not a new fact.
5. ABSTRACT COMMENTARY — sermons, morals and meta-lines in the middle of the story are removed; if the genre calls for a lesson, it is said once, at the very end.
5b. GLOSSARY, META AND SIGNPOSTS — a sentence that defines a term ("A pile is…", "Reclamation means…") is rewritten as the thing in action with its number; every mention of the film, the camera, the viewer, a chapter or a turning point is removed outright; a beat that opens on a steering connector ("Now", "So", "Then", "At this point", "By the end of") loses the connector or is cut. The order of the beats carries the logic.
5c. GENERIC SENTENCES — a line that could sit in any film about anything ("the challenge was enormous", "that changes everything") is replaced by the particular that made it so, taken from the draft or the verified facts: a number, a name, a material, a time, a consequence. Where a chapter merely continues, give it its turn — the one fact or event in the draft or the plan that contradicts what the viewer expected.
6. VOICE — keep the genre voice exactly, and keep the language of the draft ({{ $('Receive Project Data').first().json.Language }}):
{{ $('Genre Profile').first().json.p.voice }}
7. BEATS — sentences of 8-20 words, in beats of ~20-22 words, because the text is cut into 8-second scenes.
8. LABELS — the Story Bible's location labels ("Forest Starting Path", "Hilltop Finish Clearing") are pipeline names, not speech: wherever the draft says one aloud, replace it with the way a person would name the place. Character names stay.
9. FACTS — never add a fact, number, date or name that is not already in the draft{{ $('Extract Claims').first().json.claimsList ? ' or in the VERIFIED FACTS below' : '' }}; correcting a real-world error is fine, inventing is not.
{{ $('Extract Claims').first().json.claimsList ? 'VERIFIED FACTS:\n' + $('Extract Claims').first().json.claimsList + '\n' : '' }}
LENGTH: at most {{ Math.round(Math.max(1, Math.ceil($('Receive Project Data').first().json.Lenght / 8) - 1) * 22 * 1.12) }} words in total (ordered at {{ Math.max(1, Math.ceil($('Receive Project Data').first().json.Lenght / 8) - 1) * 22 }}). If the draft is long, cut description, redundancy and commentary first. If it is short, add EVENTS only where the spine or the chapter plan still holds an untold one; if they hold none, LEAVE IT SHORT — a film shorter than ordered is correct, a film padded to length is not.

OUTPUT: the complete corrected narration in the same format — the [CHAPTER n: title] marker lines exactly as in the draft (same numbers, same count, same order; a title may be improved), each followed by that chapter's narration. Plain text only — no notes, no explanations, no markdown.

DRAFT:
{{ $json.output }}
